newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr firms on weak US dlr, tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr firms on weak US dlr, tight liquidity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar, which ended at an eight-year low on Wednesday, opened sharply higher against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday, reflecting the U.S. dollar's weakness overseas and tight local liquidity, dealers said.
After 45 minutes, at 0145 GMT, the local unit was at T$27.880 against Wednesday's T$27.926 close.
Turnover was heavy at US$76 million.
Dealers said investors had turned cautious after the currency neared long-term support at T$27.94.
"The central bank used to staunchly defend the T$27.94 level, so investors have turned cautious nearing the level," said one dealer.
A tightening of liquidity due to the red-hot stock market's voracious appetite for cash also worried investors, dealers said.

The central bank said on Thursday it would issue T$13 billion in two-month negotiable certificates of deposit later in the day to mop up excess money, a move widely seen aiming to cool the stock market.
"Investors are worried that we might again see double-digit short-term interest rates if the central bank continues to tighten liquidity," the dealer said.
A T$27.860-925 range was seen for the rest of Thursday.
